name: Boarfolk
body:
Boarfolk are sometimes mistaken for wereboars, orbauks, grommuls, or pig-faced orcs—but they resent any such associations and seek to establish their own identity at every opportunity.

Physical

Boarfolk are humanoids with porcine facial features, including upright ears and piglike snouts. Many have small tusks, but not all.

Some are covered in coarse hair like boars, but others have smooth pink, gray, or black skin more reminiscent of domestic hogs.

Boarfolk feet usually have two wide toes like a pig, but some have more feet more like a humanoid. Their hands are usually human-like, however, and in any case are just as capable of manipulating tools and weapons.

Boarfolk tend to be very invested in their personal appearance, and one will almost always find them dressed in their finest clothing that the situation allows for. As a people, tattoos and piercings are taboo—although individual boarfolk have been known to adopt these practices from others.

Social

According to boarfolk legends, their ancestors were once human beings, but their hubris caused them to fall prey to a curse that gave them the appearance of the beasts whose behavior they had exhibited.

Even today, it is true that boarfolk have larger than life personalities—and the oversized egos to go along with them. At best, boarfolk are lovable heroes with hearts of gold; at worst, they’re boorish bullies who walk all over those in their way.

Boarfolk believe they are all natural leaders. While some actually are very good at this task, the fact that all boarfolk believe they are good at it makes managing any group of them very difficult.

Boarfolk communities tend to be small but proud. They are usually established near, or as part of, larger human communities. They generally get along well with all humanoids; they are quick to assume that anyone they meet is impressed with them and wants to be their new best friend—and they seem oblivious to the fact that this feeling is not always mutual.

Alignment and Religion

Boarfolk are usually Neutral. While they are very self-centered, they are not willfully cruel. They want to be in charge, but they usually have good intentions. They also want to do whatever it is that they want to do, but they also desperately want that thing to be something that will win friends and influence people. All of these conflicting motivations end up making them pretty balanced overall.

Boarfolk do not have any gods of their own.

Each boarfolk has their own religious practices, usually borrowed from the local human culture. Moreover, even though they are rarely devout, they will let you know exactly what they think about their faith and other issues of morality. In some cases, this is just a fact of their honesty and openness, while in others it is a case of passive-aggressive intolerance.

Names

Boarfolk prefer fancy-sounding names, the more ornate the better. Some typical choices include (choose or roll 1d12):

Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are personable and strong, but you don’t always put two and two together. You gain +2 Str, +2 Cha, –2 Int. [standard] (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Dwarven, Elven, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. (0)
Other Traits
Braggadocious You gain a +2 bonus on Bluff and Intimidation checks. (4)
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Fearless You gain a +2 species bonus on all saving throws against fear effects. (1)
Natural Armor You have thick skin and a protective layer of fat that provide you with a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. (2)
Pushy You gain Improved Bull Rush as a bonus feat, even if you do not meet the prerequisites. (2)
Total: 12 RP (advanced)
Alternate Traits
Big Pig You are an especially large example of your species, with both extra muscle and rolls of extra fat. Your ability score modifiers are +4 Str, –2 Dex, –2 Int. This trait alters ability score modifiers and replaces braggadocious.
Fisticuffs You gain Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. This trait replaces pushy.
Frenzy Once per day, whenever you take damage, you can fly into a frenzy for 1 minute, gaining a +2 species bonus to Constitution and Strength, but taking a –2 penalty to AC. This trait replaces pushy.
Gore Your tusks are exceptionally large, providing you with a gore attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage (1d4 if you are size Small). This trait replaces pushy.
Gregarious When you successfully use Diplomacy to win over an individual, that creature takes a –2 penalty on attempts to resist any of your Charisma-based skills for the next 24 hours. This trait replaces fearless.
Human Form The curse that affects you allows you to change back to human form, but only briefly. You can assume the appearance of a single human form once per day for up to one hour. This form is static and cannot be changed each time you take this form. You gain a +10 species bonus on Disguise checks made to appear human. Changing your shape is a standard action. This trait otherwise functions as alter self, save that you do not adjust your ability scores. This trait replaces natural armor.
Pot-Bellied You are smaller than most of your kin—in stature, that is, but certainly not in personality. You are size Small, and you gain a +2 bonus to Dexterity instead of +2 to Strength. This trait alters size and ability score modifiers.
Special Senses Scent. Your sensitive snout gives you the scent B1 universal monster ability. This trait replaces braggadocious.
Stubborn You gain a +2 species bonus on Will saving throws to resist spells and spell-like abilities of the enchantment (charm) and enchantment (compulsion) subschools. In addition, if you fail such a save, you receive another save 1 round later to prematurely end the effect (assuming the spell or spell-like ability has a duration greater than 1 round). This second save is made at the same DC as the first. If you have a similar ability from another source (such as a rogue’s slippery mind class feature), you can only use one of these abilities per round, but can try the other on the second round if the first reroll ability fails. This trait replaces pushy.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls for attacks made with unarmed strikes or natural weapons (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Bard Add a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to lie and a +1/2 bonus on Diplomacy checks to gather information.
Bloodrager Add +1 to your total number of bloodrage rounds per day.
Brawler Add +1 to the fighter’s CMD when resisting a bull rush or grapple.
Cavalier Add +1/2 to damage dealt by your mount resulting from an overrun maneuver or the trample ability.
Cleric Add a +1/2 bonus on Knowledge (nature) checks relating to creatures with the fey and monstrous humanoid types.
Fighter Add +1 to the fighter’s CMD when resisting a bull rush or sunder.
Gunslinger Add +1/4 point to your grit points.
Inquisitor Add a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple and +1/2 to the number of stunning attacks you can attempt per day.
Oracle Add a +1/3 bonus to saving throws against curse effects.
Paladin Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using smite evil (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to feint and Diplomacy checks to gather information.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Summoner Add +1 hit point to your eidolon.
Swashbuckler Increase the total number of points in your panache pool by +1/4.
